Retrieved: 2026-05-20 (Asia/Shanghai)

Title: GFT: From Imitation to Reward Fine-Tuning with Unbiased Group Advantages and Dynamic Coefficient Rectification

Authors: Wangjie Gan, Miao Pan, Linbo Xi, Wenqi Zhang, Jintao Chen, Jianwei Yin, Xuhong Zhang

- PDF: `docs/joint_training/references/external/gft_arxiv_2604_14258.pdf`

Notes for later algorithm design:

- The paper frames SFT as a special case of policy-gradient optimization with sparse implicit reward and inverse-probability weighting.
- The two main mechanisms are Group Advantage Learning and Dynamic Coefficient Rectification.
- Group Advantage Learning builds per-query response groups from expert demonstrations, teacher outputs, and self-generated samples, then uses within-group normalized reward advantages.
- Dynamic Coefficient Rectification clips/rectifies low-probability token update weights with a threshold `tau`, aiming to prevent gradient explosion while preserving knowledge-injection strength.
- The appendix contains sequence-level and token-level GFT loss formulations that are likely the most useful source material for adapting the method into the local WDL-SFT design.
